rv.q: Out on the sidewalk after the performance I saw, I smiled for blocks — smiled the next day, too, just thinking about it. Am smiling now.

Pirnot has written a play that's basically a drawing-room confessional for strapped playwrights, a work so insistently insider-y that I found myself laughing at the idea that there are enough of us to get its jokes.
Mona Pirnot’s new play I’m Assuming You Know David Greenspan is a clever and likable fan letter sealed with a kiss to a few recipients.
Greenspan accomplishes this all brilliantly, as only he alone can do it.
In the end, I will never turn down a chance to see Greenspan do what he’s so uniquely excellent at.
Crazy brilliant, and brave, is all I can say.

cn.t: Critics warmly embrace this clever meta-comedy as a delightful showcase for Greenspan's singular talent at embodying multiple characters simultaneously, with Pirnot's smart script serving as an affectionate love letter to theater itself.

vr.q: If you love theater as an art form and theater that demands that it has to be theater, I cannot recommend this enough.
